instruction: I'm accompanying a singer on harmonium tonight. How is jati used in performance?
output: For tonight's accompaniment: Jati is written with two words, first for the aroha and then for the avaroha, so audav-sampurna means five swaras going up and seven coming down, as in Raag Desh.

instruction: I'm helping a classmate revise before the viva. Any trick to remember gamak?
output: For the viva revision: Gamak sounds like its name: a heavy, deep shake.

instruction: I'm helping a classmate revise before the viva. How is samay different from prahar?
output: For the viva revision: Samay is the general idea of a raga's assigned time, while a prahar is one of the roughly three-hour watches into which the day and night are divided.

instruction: I'm helping a classmate revise before the viva. What role does andolan play when someone performs?
output: For the viva revision: Andolan is used on particular notes of certain ragas to give them their characteristic colour, and it is slow and controlled, never fast or forceful.

instruction: I'm labelling swaras in my notebook. Any trick to remember shruti?
output: For your notebook: Shruti comes from 'hearing'. It is the smallest difference you can hear.

instruction: I'm labelling swaras in my notebook. How is badhat used in performance?
output: For your notebook: Badhat describes the growth of a performance: a raga is not shown all at once but opened up gradually. Badhat is how a raga's form is revealed to the listener; the same raga can be shown well or poorly depending on how its development is paced.

instruction: I'm labelling swaras in my notebook. What is the difference between kan swara and meend?
output: For your notebook: A kan swara is a quick touch of an adjacent note, while meend is a continuous slide that covers the whole interval between two notes.

instruction: I'm listening to a recording and want to follow along. How is kan swara different from gamak?
output: To follow along: A kan swara is a light, fleeting touch of a neighbouring note, while gamak is a heavy, weighty oscillation.

instruction: I'm listening to a recording and want to follow along. Is thaat a note or an ornament or something else?
output: To follow along: Thaat is a classification concept, not a performed entity.

instruction: I'm listening to a recording and want to follow along. Where would I hear jati?
output: To follow along: Raag Bhupali is audav-audav (five swaras both ways), Raag Marwa is shadav-shadav and Raag Yaman is sampurna-sampurna. Raag Khamaj is shadav-sampurna, because it leaves Re out of the aroha.

instruction: I'm making flashcards for revision. Can you give an example of jati?
output: For your flashcards: Raag Bhupali is audav-audav (five swaras both ways), Raag Marwa is shadav-shadav and Raag Yaman is sampurna-sampurna.

instruction: I'm making flashcards for revision. What is the difference between thaat and raga?
output: For your flashcards: A thaat is a classificatory scale, while a raga is a performable melodic framework with its own phrases, vadi, samvadi and mood.

instruction: I'm making flashcards for revision. Why should I learn badhat?
output: For your flashcards: Badhat is how a raga's form is revealed to the listener; the same raga can be shown well or poorly depending on how its development is paced.

instruction: I'm planning a practice session for my sitar students. Why does meend matter in raga?
output: For your students: Much of a raga's shape is heard in how the notes are joined, and meend is one of the main ways of joining them smoothly.

instruction: I'm preparing a short talk for my college music society. Any trick to remember samay?
output: For your talk: Samay is 'time' in Hindi: when the raga is sung.

instruction: I'm preparing a short talk for my college music society. Can you give an example of gamak?
output: For your talk: Fast, heavy shakes on a note in a slow, serious phrase are an example of gamak. It is heard wherever a performer wants weight on a swara.

instruction: I'm preparing a short talk for my college music society. Is kan swara a note or an ornament or something else?
output: For your talk: Kan swara is an ornamentation, like a grace note in western terms.

instruction: I'm preparing a short talk for my college music society. What does andolan mean in hindustani music?
output: For your talk: Andolan is a slow, gentle oscillation of a note that stays within that note's own pitch region (shruti). Andolan is used on particular notes of certain ragas to give them their characteristic colour, and it is slow and controlled, never fast or forceful.

instruction: I'm preparing a short talk for my college music society. What does kan swara mean in hindustani music?
output: For your talk: A kan swara is a grace note: a brief touch of a neighbouring swara just before or after the main note. Kan is used to colour a note and make a phrase more graceful. It is too short to register as a separate note on its own.

instruction: I'm preparing for my music exam tomorrow. What is thaat?
output: For your exam: A thaat is a parent scale used to classify ragas in Hindustani music; it is the Hindustani counterpart of the melakarta idea in Carnatic music.

instruction: I'm transcribing a bandish and want to check my notes. Can you explain meend in simple words?
output: For your transcription: Meend is sliding smoothly from one swara to the next instead of jumping, a bit like sliding a finger along a string.

instruction: I'm transcribing a bandish and want to check my notes. How is gamak different from meend?
output: For your transcription: Gamak is an oscillation on a note, while meend is a smooth glide from one note to another.

instruction: I'm transcribing a bandish and want to check my notes. What role does samay play when someone performs?
output: For your transcription: Samay is counted in prahars, the roughly three-hour watches of the day and night, and teachers traditionally say a raga is best performed within its slot.

instruction: I'm transcribing a bandish and want to check my notes. Where would I hear kan swara?
output: For your transcription: Touching Re very lightly before landing on Ga is an example: the Re is the kan swara and Ga is the main note. It is used across many ragas wherever a phrase is decorated by a light touch of a neighbouring swara.

instruction: I'm transcribing a bandish and want to check my notes. Why does gamak matter in raga?
output: For your transcription: Gamak gives a raga weight and gravity, so it matters in how serious ragas are voiced.

instruction: I'm writing programme notes for a concert. How is shruti different from swara?
output: For your programme notes: A swara is one of the named notes (Sa, Re, Ga and so on), while shrutis are the finer pitch positions within the octave from which the swaras are placed.

instruction: I'm writing programme notes for a concert. Where would I hear badhat?
output: For your programme notes: In a vocal alap a singer introduces the raga slowly and then extends it to higher swaras, stage by stage, which is badhat. It is part of every raga performance.

instruction: I'm writing programme notes for a concert. Why does jati matter in raga?
output: For your programme notes: Jati tells you at a glance how many notes you can use in each direction, which is the first check when learning a raga.

instruction: My guru quizzed me in class today and I blanked. How is gamak used in performance?
output: For next class: Gamak is most associated with serious, weighty styles of singing and playing, where the oscillation is produced with force and gives the phrase depth. Gamak gives a raga weight and gravity, so it matters in how serious ragas are voiced.

instruction: My guru quizzed me in class today and I blanked. How is thaat different from raga?
output: For next class: A thaat is a classificatory scale, while a raga is a performable melodic framework with its own phrases, vadi, samvadi and mood.

instruction: My guru quizzed me in class today and I blanked. Is badhat a note or an ornament or something else?
output: For next class: Badhat is a performance concept.

instruction: My guru quizzed me in class today and I blanked. What is the difference between andolan and meend?
output: For next class: Andolan stays on one note and sways around it, whereas meend carries the voice from one note to another.

instruction: My niece just started learning and asked me. What is the difference between andolan and gamak?
output: To explain it to your niece: Andolan is a slow, gentle oscillation, while gamak is forceful and heavy.

instruction: My niece just started learning and asked me. What kind of thing is thaat?
output: To explain it to your niece: Thaat is a classification concept, not a performed entity.

instruction: My teacher asked me to prepare a raga for Saturday's class. Any trick to remember badhat?
output: For Saturday's class: Badhat comes from the idea of 'growing'.

instruction: My teacher asked me to prepare a raga for Saturday's class. How is andolan different from gamak?
output: For Saturday's class: Andolan is a slow, gentle oscillation, while gamak is forceful and heavy.

instruction: My teacher asked me to prepare a raga for Saturday's class. How would you explain jati to a beginner?
output: For Saturday's class: Jati is a swara count. If a raga uses five notes it is audav, six is shadav and seven is sampurna.

instruction: My teacher asked me to prepare a raga for Saturday's class. What is shruti?
output: For Saturday's class: A shruti is the smallest interval of pitch the human ear can detect, and the octave is conventionally divided into 22 of them. Shruti is used in theory to explain how the seven swaras sit within the octave and why a note can be sung slightly higher or lower in different ragas. The 22-shruti figure is conventional; historical sources disagree on the exact values.

instruction: My teacher asked me to prepare a raga for Saturday's class. What is the difference between thaat and jati?
output: For Saturday's class: A thaat is a seven-note parent scale that groups ragas, while jati classifies a single raga by how many swaras its aroha and avaroha use.

instruction: My teacher asked me to prepare a raga for Saturday's class. What role does jati play when someone performs?
output: For Saturday's class: Jati is written with two words, first for the aroha and then for the avaroha, so audav-sampurna means five swaras going up and seven coming down, as in Raag Desh.

instruction: Someone at a concert asked me this and I wasn't sure. Can you explain samay in simple words?
output: For next time someone asks: Samay means the time a raga belongs to: some are for the morning, some for dusk, some for deep night. Sources differ on the exact slot for some ragas, and in modern concerts the rule is applied loosely.

instruction: Someone at a concert asked me this and I wasn't sure. Is meend a note or an ornament or something else?
output: For next time someone asks: Meend is an ornamentation: a way of decorating or connecting notes, not a note or a scale.

instruction: Someone at a concert asked me this and I wasn't sure. What role does badhat play when someone performs?
output: For next time someone asks: Badhat describes the growth of a performance: a raga is not shown all at once but opened up gradually.
